source_caption:
Valerie and Her Week of Wonders (1970) is a visually striking Czechoslovak fantasy film directed by Jaromil Jireš, part of the Czech New Wave, and based on a novel by poet Vítězslav Nezval. Starring Jaroslava Schallerová, it follows Valerie through a strange, dreamlike week in a village filled with folklore, rituals, and surreal encounters.

On the surface it feels like a dark fairytale, but underneath it’s really about growing up. The film explores identity, innocence, and the shift from childhood to adolescence, using symbolism and imagination instead of a straightforward, realistic story.

source_details.synopsis: Valerie and Her Week of Wonders (Czech: Valerie a týden divů) is a 1970 Czechoslovak Gothic coming-of-age surrealist dark fantasy horror film co-written and directed by Jaromil Jireš, based on the 1935 novel by Vítězslav Nezval. It is considered one of the last films of the Czechoslovak New Wave movement. The film portrays the heroine as living in a disorienting dream, cajoled by priests, vampires, and men and women alike. The film blends dark fantasy, eroticism and Gothic horror genres.
